newProposals.before: Thereafter Shi Hu fell and the Central Plain turned toward civilization; generals and ministers were content.
newProposals.after: Thereafter Shi Jilong fell and the Central Plain turned toward civilization; generals and ministers were content.
newProposals.reason: Literal must name 石季龍 as Shi Jilong (same person as idiomatic), not Shi Hu.

newProposals.before: A six-month drought forced rites at every shrine from ancestors to rivers.
newProposals.after: In the ninth year drought lasted from the first month through the sixth, and they prayed at the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and the mountains and rivers.
newProposals.reason: Restore ninth-year drought span (正月–六月) and the three prayer sites 宗廟/社稷/山川 omitted by the summary idiom.

newProposals.before: The sites all tied to Wu and the future emperor.
newProposals.after: Qu'a too was once Wu land; that the omen appeared at Wu Xiong's residence in a Wu town — was that not also Heaven's will?
newProposals.reason: Restore 曲阿, 吳邑雄 (Wu Xiong), and the 天意 rhetorical question; drop invented "future emperor".

amendedDecisions.priorHold: idiomatic inserted toward Jin for 向化
amendedDecisions.after: After Shi Jilong's fall the Central Plain turned toward civilization and generals and ministers were content.
amendedDecisions.reason: Hold resolution: source names 石季龍; 中原向化 is assimilation/submission toward civilization, not a lexical "Jin".
